newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bratislava bourse pushes higher on Slovnaft gains.
newsitem.headline: Bratislava bourse pushes higher on Slovnaft gains.

text.p: Slovak shares closed mostly higher in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, as the SAX index edged up 4.77 points to 178.82 on gains to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft.
Brokers said that despite thinner activity, they were seeing higher demand, mainly from the side of foreign investors, that is expected to push the bourse higher in the coming days.
"The market seems to be waking up, but there is still a danger that relatively high demand will not meet the offer and trading could freeze," Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt said.

Slovnaft, the most-capitalised issue on the BSE, closed down 80 crowns at 700, but its average price, on which the index is calculated, was 9.55 percent higher. Steel maker VSZ closed up 50 crowns at 610.
"Another problem is that there are still only a few shares traded," Krutil said. "Although those (issues) that traded posted gains, three or four issues are not enough to initiate a stronger trend."
Overall volume increased to 1,167,631 shares, from 269,299 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover rose to 465.24 million crowns, from 354.21 million.
